text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager — Meridian (enterprise-vpc) detected sudden prefix prefetch storm and KV cache hit-rate collapse in dedicated pool meridian-prod-1. Severity: P1. Affected routes: /generate, /chat. Notifying on-call.
Alex: I'm on it. Seeing huge increases in KV store ops for tenant meridian-corp, spike from ~200r/s -> 12kr/s. Prefetch workers are saturating CPU on n1-gpu nodes.
Maya: Paging in. Can you paste the prefetch config for that tenant?
Alex: Tenant config excerpt: ```
tenant: meridian-corp
kv_prefetch:
  enabled: true
  concurrency: 32
  lookahead: 6
  per_prefix_limit: 10000
```
Jen: That per_prefix_limit is huge. Looks like a recent customer request to improve latency for long-tail prompts. Might be flooding cache with large prefix sets.
Sam: Logs from the runtime showing repeated prefix eviction + re-warm: ```
[2026-03-15T10:22:09Z] prefix_evict: prefix="m-usr-123" reason=memory_pressure
[2026-03-15T10:22:09Z] prefetch_request: prefix="m-usr-123" size=820
[2026-03-15T10:22:09Z] prefetch_complete: prefix="m-usr-123" latency_ms=120
[2026-03-15T10:22:10Z] prefix_evict: prefix="m-usr-456" reason=memory_pressure
... (repeats thousands of times)```
Gina: Meridian tenant reported latency spikes in their support channel. They see increased 5xxs on /chat. This is customer-impacting.
Alex: Impact assessment: ~18% p50 latency increase on /generate for Meridian users, ~3% errors due to timeouts on chat route across the dedicated pool. No cross-tenant errors observed yet but risk high.
Maya: Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) throttle prefetch concurrency for that tenant 2) temporarily disable tenant-prefetch and fallback to on-demand caching 3) scale pool or move a subset of traffic to a cold fallback region. Which should we attempt first?
Alex: Do #1 and #2 in parallel: reduce concurrency to 4 and set kv_prefetch.enabled=false for the tenant. That should stop the storm quickly. I'll apply changes via infra tool.
Jen: Leave a canary first? If we disable prefetch we might regress their tail latency but reduce CPU churn. Given customer impact, do global disable for that tenant immediately.
Sam: Executing change: ```
$ infractl tenant update meridian-corp --set kv_prefetch.enabled=false --set kv_prefetch.concurrency=4
Applying to dedicated pool: meridian-prod-1
OK: update accepted, rolling to nodes
```
IncidentBot: Deployment started (job id jb-88221). Rolling config to 8 nodes in meridian-prod-1. Estimated roll time 2m.
Alex: Observability: dropping KV ops now from 12kr/s -> 450r/s within 60s. Eviction logs tailing down.
Gina: Meridian confirms tail latency reduced on their end, but they're seeing a few longer cold-start responses. They want ETA for full recovery.
Maya: Recovery ETA 10–15m for metrics to stabilize and errors to fall under 0.5%. Keep customer updated: "We throttled tenant prefetching to stop the cache thrash, restoring stability; some infrequent cold starts may occur as the cache rebuilds."
Jen: Follow-up mitigation: schedule per-tenant cache caps and prefetch budgets. Also we should implement a hard upper bound on per_prefix_limit and a guardrail that rejects config values above X.
Alex: Agreed. I'll open a PR for runtime validation: reject concurrency > 16 and per_prefix_limit > 2000 for dedicated pools unless enterprise-approved with SRE signoff.
Sam: Noting we also need a temporary routing fallback if pool starts to saturate again — route Meridian to meridian-standby (smaller model or quantized) after 90s of sustained error rate >1%. Add to runbook.
Maya: On-call handoff: Alex will continue the mitigation and monitoring for the next 30m, then handoff to me at 11:00 UTC.
Alex: Oncall -> Maya at 11:00 UTC. Current status: mitigated (prefetch disabled), hit-rate improving, error rate trending down from 3% -> 0.6%.
Jen: Action items: 1) PR for validation + guardrails (Alex) 2) Runbook update with automatic fallback policy (Sam) 3) Post-incident with customer timeline and config diff (Gina) 4) Telemetry alert to detect per-tenant prefetch spikes (Maya).
Gina: I'll draft the customer communication: quick note explaining root cause (overaggressive prefetch config caused cache churn and evictions), what we changed, and the next steps. Will include short-term workaround and timeline for guardrail rollout.
IncidentBot: Pager resolved at 1945010600. Root cause: misconfigured tenant prefetch settings combined with per-node memory pressure.
Maya: Leaving a pinned log snippet in the incident channel and will take the postmortem cadence. Jen — can you triage whether the dedicated pool should have stricter defaults?
Jen: Yes, I'll run a config audit across dedicated pools and propose safer defaults.
Alex: Handoff complete. I'll keep monitoring for 1h then follow postmortem actions.
Gina: Meridian accepted the message and requested a brief call tomorrow to review changes. Scheduling now.
Maya: Thanks team. Closing active loop; will file incident report with timelines and config diffs. :white_check_mark:
